analysis.title: GS Bartlett - GS TMT TODAY 10.16.26
key_insights: US futures mixed (NDX -15bps, SPX +10bps, RTY +15bps) as global markets stabilize after a volatile session on 10/15. KOSPI rose 2% to snap a seven-day losing streak but is still on track for a weekly loss of about 14%, its worst in over three months (Bloomberg).
The Stoxx 600 is on track for its biggest weekly outperformance over the S&P since March.

Warsh said at the IMF meeting that he does not 'prejudge meetings' and gave no hawkish guidance ahead of the October meeting. Odds of an October hike fell from about 30% to about 17%. The Fed enters its blackout period 10/17.

Pre-market AI-complex names are indicated lower: CRWV -4%, memory names -2%, SMH -1%. Other movers: NFLX -2.5% on a new content chief, TSLA +4% on the Roadster demonstration, ZETA +6% on a GS upgrade, KVYO -1.5% on a GS downgrade, MSFT +50bps on a GIR earnings preview.
Netflix is replacing chief creative officer Bela Bajaria with Peter Rice (ex-Disney, ex-21st Century Fox), effective Oct. 26, to reverse a slowdown in viewers and revenue (Bloomberg).

Tesla unveiled its long-delayed Roadster on Thursday in a demonstration using air thrusters developed with SpaceX engineers. It will sit in a slimmed-down lineup built mainly around two mid-priced models (Bloomberg).

MSFT reports 1QFY (September) results on 10/28. The stock is up 38% since the 7/29 4Q report versus the Nasdaq up 10%. GS (Borges) sees a reasonable upside case of Azure growth of 46-47% cc versus 44-45% cc guidance, and 2QFY guidance of about 46-47% cc.

GS (Borges) sees potential M365 Commercial Cloud growth of about 17-18% cc in 1QFY versus 17% cc guidance. Maia 200 is in production and Maia 300 is expected in 2027, which GS expects to support gross margin over time through more in-house silicon. GS calls MSFT the best positioned name in its Software coverage.

GS Global Credit Trader (Lynam): higher rates have raised questions about AI capex funding and caused a correction in some risk assets, most visibly in USD HY. Index-level spreads remain relatively supported but dispersion is elevated. GS stays underweight USD IG Technology and neutral USD HY.

USD IG and HY project finance issuance year to date has passed $106B, nearly triple the $37B in 2025. GS says risks to its 2027 global forecast of $300B are skewed firmly to the upside. HY datacenter bond average dollar prices fell from above $101 in June to nearly $95.

Macro: US 10-year yield is a touch higher at 5.09% and crude is flat. Semis, memory and AI-related names are under pressure (SMH -50bps, DRAM -1.5%, CRWV -4%). Bowman said she does not feel urgency for further action. Import Price Index is due at 8:30am and Industrial Production at 9:15am.
Asia closed higher: Shanghai +24bps, Hang Seng +52bps, Nikkei +1.39%, Kospi +2.05%. Europe is higher: FTSE +15bps, DAX +1.1%, CAC +50bps, with tech and financials outperforming and energy lagging.

Flex closed the $4.4B EPC Power deal on 10/14. FLEX shares are down 18% week to date versus JBL -6% and VRT -12%. Its investor day is 11/10 in Austin, and it plans to spin off its Cloud & Power Infrastructure segment as Axiom in 1QCY27.
GS upgraded ZETA to Buy from Neutral and downgraded KVYO to Neutral from Buy. ZETA is up 65% YTD, and GS sees upside to 2027 estimates and a 4x risk/reward skew for ZETA.

CXMT announced progress on a new DRAM cell architecture called '4F2' on October 10 and said it plans a new server-memory product on it by end of 2026. GS published a note on the implications for Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.
Street actions: MBLY initiated at Buy (Citi), WDAY downgraded to Sector Weight (KeyBanc). AXP reports pre-market. Pre-open earnings also include CFG, MTB, RF, TFC and TRV.
